inspiration: A creature built part by part, with dependencies: 16_Bug/README.md line 5 describes a bug drawn part by part from die rolls, where each part needs the one before (body, then neck, then head). The reveal order is the idea: a creature that assembles in a fixed sequence builds anticipation.

A shy creature in a tiny arena: 51_Hurkle/README.md line 5 hides a creature on a 10 by 10 grid, with homebase in a corner, and the player finds it with hints. A small hidden beast in a bounded map is a good mood for a side quest.

A guesser that learns: 03_Animal/README.md line 3 describes a game where the computer asks questions and, after a miss, asks the player for a new question to add to its tree. An NPC that grows its own question list from player answers is a clear design lift.

A yearly ledger screen: 43_Hammurabi/README.md line 3 frames a city-management game where each year trades land, grain and population. The turn report reads as a compact status screen, a good HUD model for a settlement view.

Centred title plus publisher line: the programs open with a centred title and a credit line (19_Bunny/bunny.bas lines 1-2 use TAB to centre the title and a publisher line). A simple title card with a credit line works for any retro menu.
Known Bugs and Porting Notes sections: the Acey Ducey README (01_Acey_Ducey/README.md) records known defects and port differences next to the game. Useful as a template for our own content docs.

briefs.label: Part-by-part beast
briefs.why: A creature that is assembled in a fixed order builds anticipation and shows its anatomy as it appears.
briefs.keep: Ordered dependencies (base, then joint, then head); a pace set by a dice-like roll; each part visibly locks in.
briefs.change: A bulky crawler whose armour plates gate its parts, not a bug; ornaments come first; a glow that grows as parts lock in.

briefs.label: Hidden grid beast
briefs.why: A small, odd creature hidden in a bounded area gives a clear search loop and a memorable find.
briefs.keep: A shy creature hiding in a tiny arena; hints that narrow the search; a home corner.
briefs.change: A glowing pack animal with a call sound; a real map instead of a numbered grid; a silhouette that gives hints by shape.

briefs.label: Learning riddle spirit
briefs.why: A guesser that grows its own question list makes an NPC feel like it remembers the player.
briefs.keep: A question tree that gains a new question after a miss; a tone of gentle guessing.
briefs.change: A spirit made of drifting motes that remembers answers per player; the questions come from the world, not a fixed list.

briefs.label: Yearly ledger screen
briefs.why: A short turn report with a few numbers and a choice each turn gives a clear management loop.
briefs.keep: Turn-based yearly report; trade-offs between land, food and people.
briefs.change: A visual ledger on a village map instead of text; our own resource set and themes.
